## Overview

This document records every change made to the **forestsearch** package in response
to the CRAN pre-submission review. For each issue the reviewer raised, the relevant
CRAN policy is cited, the location of the problem in the codebase is identified, and
the specific fix applied is described.

Eight distinct issues were addressed across 17 files.

---

## Fix 1 — `DESCRIPTION`: Quotes around acronyms and excess whitespace {#fix1}

**File:** `DESCRIPTION`

### Issue

The CRAN reviewer flagged two problems:

1. Single quotes (`'GRF'`, `'MRCT'`, `'AFT'`) were used around acronyms in the
   `Description` field. CRAN's writing guide specifies that single quotes in
   `Description` are reserved exclusively for *package names* (e.g., `'ggplot2'`).
   Acronyms and technical abbreviations must appear bare.

2. The multi-line `Description` field had excessive internal whitespace. Each
   hard-wrapped continuation line is parsed with a leading space, so unnecessary
   line breaks introduce extraneous spaces in the final parsed description.

### Fix

```diff
- using machine learning approaches including Generalized Random Forests ('GRF'),
- LASSO regularization, and exhaustive combinatorial search algorithms. ...
- particularly for multi-regional clinical trials ('MRCT') requiring regional
- ... Supports both accelerated failure time ('AFT') and Cox ...
+ using machine learning approaches including Generalized Random Forests (GRF),
+ LASSO regularization, and exhaustive combinatorial search algorithms. ...
+ particularly for multi-regional clinical trials (MRCT) requiring regional
+ ... Supports both accelerated failure time (AFT) and Cox ...
```

The paragraph was also tightened to reduce line count and avoid extra spaces.

### Reference

[CRAN Repository Policy — Package descriptions](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/R-exts.html#The-DESCRIPTION-file)

## Fix 2 — `options(warn = -1)` in `bootstrap_dofuture_main.R` {#fix2}

**File:** `R/bootstrap_dofuture_main.R`  
**Function:** `forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture()`

### Issue

The function globally suppressed all warnings for the duration of its bootstrap
section using `options(warn = -1)`. CRAN policy prohibits setting `options(warn)`
inside package functions because doing so silently discards warnings for *all* code
running during that period — including code the user may have written — without their
knowledge or consent. The policy states:

> *"You are setting options(warn=-1) in your function. This is not allowed. Please
> rather use `suppressWarnings()` if really needed."*

A secondary problem was that the same restore line appeared twice: once inside the
`on.exit()` handler (correct) and once as an explicit call after
`bootstrap_results()` (redundant and fragile — it would be skipped if an error
occurred before reaching it).

### Before

```r
old_warn <- getOption("warn")
options(warn = -1)                   # globally suppress all warnings

on.exit({
  options(warn = old_warn)           # restore in on.exit
  future::plan("sequential")
  ...
}, add = TRUE)

results <- bootstrap_results(...)

options(warn = old_warn)             # redundant second restore
```

### Fix

Both the `options(warn = -1)` call and all associated save/restore lines were
removed. The `on.exit()` handler was retained for future plan restoration and
garbage collection only. Any specific calls within the bootstrap machinery that
genuinely produce expected warnings should use `suppressWarnings()` scoped to
that call alone.

```r
on.exit({
  if (exists(".Last.future.plan")) {
    future::plan(.Last.future.plan)
  } else {
    future::plan("sequential")
  }
  if (exists("Ystar_mat") && object.size(Ystar_mat) > 1e9) {
    gc(verbose = FALSE, reset = TRUE)
  }
}, add = TRUE)
```

### Reference

[CRAN Cookbook — Setting options(warn = -1)](https://contributor.r-project.org/cran-cookbook/code_issues.html#setting-optionswarn--1)

## Fix 3 — `par()` not restored in `subgroup_consistency_helpers.R` {#fix3}

**File:** `R/subgroup_consistency_helpers.R`  
**Function:** `plot_subgroup()`

### Issue

The internal `plot_subgroup()` helper called `par(mfrow = c(1, 2))` to set a
two-panel layout for weighted Kaplan–Meier plots, but never saved or restored the
user's previous `par()` settings. CRAN policy requires that package functions
*immediately* save graphical parameters with `on.exit()` before modifying them, so
that the user's environment is restored even if the function exits via an error.

> *"Please make sure that you do not change the user's options, par or working
> directory. If you really have to do so within functions, please ensure with an
> immediate call of `on.exit()` that the settings are reset when the function
> is exited."*

### Before

```r
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
weightedsurv::plot_weighted_km(dfcount,  ...)
weightedsurv::plot_weighted_km(dfcountC, ...)
```

### Fix

```r
oldpar <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
on.exit(par(oldpar), add = TRUE)
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
weightedsurv::plot_weighted_km(dfcount,  ...)
weightedsurv::plot_weighted_km(dfcountC, ...)
```

The `add = TRUE` argument to `on.exit()` is important — it *appends* the restore
to any existing exit handlers rather than replacing them.

### Reference

[CRAN Cookbook — Change of graphical parameters](https://contributor.r-project.org/cran-cookbook/code_issues.html#change-of-options-graphical-parameters-and-working-directory)

## Fix 4 — Writing to user's home filespace in `cox_ahr_cde_wrapper.R` {#fix4}

**File:** `R/cox_ahr_cde_wrapper.R`  
**Function:** `cox_ahr_cde_analysis()`

### Issue

The `output_dir` parameter defaulted to `"plots"`, a relative path that resolves
to a `plots/` subdirectory of the user's current working directory. When
`save_plots = TRUE` is used, the function calls `dir.create(output_dir)`, which
creates a directory in the user's filespace without their explicit consent. CRAN
policy prohibits functions from writing to the user's home filespace or working
directory by default.

> *"Please ensure that your functions do not write by default or in your
> examples/vignettes/tests in the user's home filespace (including the package
> directory and getwd()). Please omit any default path in writing functions.
> In your examples/vignettes/tests you can write to `tempdir()`."*

### Before

```r
cox_ahr_cde_analysis <- function(
    ...,
    save_plots = FALSE,
    output_dir = "plots",    # resolves to getwd()/plots/
    ...
)
```

### Fix

```r
cox_ahr_cde_analysis <- function(
    ...,
    save_plots = FALSE,
    output_dir = tempdir(),  # safe temporary location
    ...
)
```

The `@param` documentation was updated to match. Because `save_plots` defaults to
`FALSE`, no directory is created during a normal call; this fix only affects
behaviour when the user explicitly requests plot saving.

### Reference

[CRAN Cookbook — Writing files to the home filespace](https://contributor.r-project.org/cran-cookbook/code_issues.html#writing-files-and-directories-to-the-home-filespace)

## Fix 5 — `par()` not restored in vignette (`forestsearch.Rmd`) {#fix5}

**File:** `vignettes/forestsearch.Rmd`  
**Chunk:** `grf-trees`

### Issue

The vignette chunk that plots GRF policy trees called `par(mfrow = c(1, 2))` and
then manually reset with `par(mfrow = c(1, 1))` at the end of the chunk. CRAN
requires that vignettes (like functions) restore graphical parameters using
`on.exit()` so that the reset occurs even if the chunk exits unexpectedly.

> *"Please always make sure to reset to user's options(), working directory or
> par() after you changed it in examples and vignettes."*

### Before

```r
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot(grf_est$tree1, ...)
plot(grf_est$tree2, ...)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))   # manual reset — skipped if an error occurs above
```

### Fix

```r
oldpar <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
on.exit(par(oldpar), add = TRUE)
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot(grf_est$tree1, ...)
plot(grf_est$tree2, ...)
# manual reset removed — on.exit handles it
```

### Reference

[CRAN Cookbook — Change of graphical parameters](https://contributor.r-project.org/cran-cookbook/code_issues.html#change-of-options-graphical-parameters-and-working-directory)

## Fix 6 — `\dontrun{}` replaced with `\donttest{}` throughout {#fix6}

**Files:** All 48 R source files  
**Count:** 105 occurrences converted

### Issue

`\dontrun{}` appeared in the `@examples` block of every exported function in the
package. This wrapping causes the examples to appear in the documentation as
`# Not run:` comments — misleading to users and flagged by CRAN reviewers as
equivalent to "commented-out code":

> *"`\dontrun{}` should only be used if the example really cannot be executed
> (e.g. because of missing additional software, missing API keys, ...). Please
> replace `\dontrun{}` with `\donttest{}`."*

The distinction matters:

| Wrapper | When to use | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `\donttest{}` | Example is correct but slow (> 5 sec) | Runs in extended checks; skipped on CRAN's servers |
| `\dontrun{}` | Example genuinely cannot run (missing software, credentials) | Never runs; shown as `# Not run:` in docs |

Every example in `forestsearch` *can* be executed — they are simply slow because
they invoke the full ForestSearch algorithm. `\donttest{}` is therefore the correct
wrapper.

### Fix

A global substitution was applied across all R source files:

```bash
sed -i "s/#' \\dontrun{/#' \\donttest{/g" R/*.R
```

### Reference

[CRAN Cookbook — Structuring of examples](https://contributor.r-project.org/cran-cookbook/general_issues.html#structuring-of-examples)

## Fix 7 — Missing `\value` tags in 13 `.Rd` files {#fix7}

**Files:** 8 R source files  
**Functions:** 13

### Issue

CRAN requires a `\value` section (generated from `@return` in roxygen2) in every
`.Rd` file for exported functions, documenting what the function returns. This
applies even to functions called for side effects, which should state:

```
\value{No return value, called for side effects}
```

The reviewer flagged 13 missing `\value` tags. These fell into three categories:

| Category | Functions | Return text |
|---|---|---|
| Complex list-returning functions | `generate_aft_dgm_flex`, `get_FSdata` | Named list with itemised components |
| Side-effect-only (plot/print to console) | `plot_spline_treatment_effect`, `print_grf_details` | No return value, called for side effects |
| S3 print/plot methods | All others below | Invisibly returns `x` |

The full list of functions fixed:

| File | Function | Fix applied |
|---|---|---|
| `generate_aft_dgm_main.R` | `generate_aft_dgm_flex` | Named list description |
| `get_fsdata.R` | `get_FSdata` | Named list description |
| `generate_aft_dgm_helpers_outcome.R` | `plot_spline_treatment_effect` | Side effects |
| `render_forestplot.R` | `print.fs_forest_theme` | Invisibly returns `x` |
| `render_forestplot.R` | `print.fs_forestplot` | Invisibly returns `x` |
| `render_forestplot.R` | `plot.fs_forestplot` | Invisibly returns `x` |
| `plot_sg_results.R` | `print.fs_sg_plot` | Invisibly returns `x` |
| `plot_sg_results.R` | `plot.fs_sg_plot` | Invisibly returns `x` |
| `plot_sg_weighted_km.R` | `print.fs_weighted_km` | Invisibly returns `x` |
| `forestsearch_cross_validation.R` | `print.fs_kfold` | Invisibly returns `x` |
| `forestsearch_cross_validation.R` | `print.fs_tenfold` | Invisibly returns `x` |
| `grf_helpers.R` | `print_grf_details` | Side effects |
| `sim_aft_gbsg.R` | `print.gbsg_dgm` | Invisibly returns `x` |

### Example fix (S3 print method)

```r
#' @param x An fs_kfold object
#' @param ... Additional arguments (ignored)
#' @return Invisibly returns \code{x}.   # <-- added
#' @examples
```

### Reference

[CRAN Cookbook — Missing value tags in .Rd files](https://contributor.r-project.org/cran-cookbook/docs_issues.html#missing-value-tags-in-.rd-files)

## Fix 8 — Examples for unexported functions {#fix8}

**Files:** 4 R source files  
**Functions:** 4

### Issue

Four functions had `@examples` blocks in their roxygen documentation but were not
exported (they carried `@keywords internal`). CRAN does not run examples for
unexported functions, so the presence of `@examples` is either misleading or an
error. The reviewer flagged:

> *"You have examples for unexported functions. Please either omit these examples
> or export these functions."*

The four functions were:

| Function | Source file |
|---|---|
| `create_sample_size_table` | `R/truefind_asymptotic.R` |
| `detect_variable_types` | `R/synthetic_data_perturbation.R` |
| `extract_selected_tree_cuts` | `R/grf_helpers.R` |
| `find_quantile_for_proportion` | `R/find_k_inter_main.R` |

All four are already listed in `_pkgdown.yml` as documented reference functions and
have fully self-contained, informative examples. The appropriate resolution is
therefore to **export them** rather than remove the examples.

### Fix

For each function, `@keywords internal` was replaced with `@export`:

```r
# Before
#' @keywords internal
create_sample_size_table <- function(...) { ... }

# After
#' @export
create_sample_size_table <- function(...) { ... }
```

After running `devtools::document()`, the NAMESPACE will gain four new `export()`
entries:

```
export(create_sample_size_table)
export(detect_variable_types)
export(extract_selected_tree_cuts)
export(find_quantile_for_proportion)
```

### Reference

[CRAN Cookbook — Examples for unexported functions](https://contributor.r-project.org/cran-cookbook/docs_issues.html)

---

## Post-fix workflow

After copying all corrected files into the package, run the standard sequence:

```r
devtools::document()          # regenerates man/ and NAMESPACE
devtools::load_all()          # load updated package
devtools::check_built(args = "--as-cran")
```

Then retest on win-builder before resubmitting:

- <https://win-builder.r-project.org/> (R-devel and R-release)
- Submission portal: <https://cran.r-project.org/submit.html>

The one pre-existing NOTE about the time server (`unable to verify current time`)
is a local network condition unrelated to the package and should remain documented
in `cran-comments.md` as before.
